plate.purpose: Runs column and default day arc ground (base2 / base02).

paper.purpose: Output, Settings, command well, menu bar popover (base3 / base03).

ink.purpose: Primary and log text; next-run ring on the arc.

muted.purpose: Secondary text, timestamps, durations, arc labels.

hairline.purpose: 1pt separators and the command well border.

horizon.purpose: Arc horizon line and dotted full-day path.

sun.purpose: Succeeded glyph, passed marks, elapsed arc path, sun body, menu hover wash.

sunlight.purpose: Fixed in all appearances; translucent daylight fill and log selection only.

sky.purpose: Running glyph, running ring, running header wash.

ember.purpose: App accent via AccentColor asset; selection and control tint only.

storm.purpose: Failed and interrupted glyphs, failure diamonds, failure header wash.

storm-text.purpose: Failure text: exit codes, Failed title, result values, errors.

dusk.purpose: Never-run glyph and the moon on the arc.

title.purpose: Run status in the output header and the app name in Settings; macOS title2, rounded semibold.

headline.purpose: Day arc title in the menu bar popover; rounded.

caption.purpose: Arc summary, arc hour labels (caption2), header field labels.

gradients.name: status-wash
gradients.purpose: Behind the output header; tint is sun, sky, or storm by run state.

gradients.name: daylight
gradients.purpose: Day arc fill above the horizon, top of arc to horizon.

motion.name: running-rays
motion.purpose: Running status glyph; disabled under Reduce Motion.

motion.name: arc-tick
motion.purpose: Day arc and relative times refresh each minute; durations of live runs each second.

components.name: Status Icon
components.description: Weather glyph per run state: sun passed, storm cloud failed, cloud interrupted, rotating rays running, horizon never run.

narrative.overview:
Sundial is a native Mac utility dressed as a day of weather. Healthy runs are sunshine, failures are storms, and the runs column opens on the sun's path across the day. The palette is Solarized: cream plate and paper grounds in light, deep teal base03/base02 in dark, with the sun's yellow carrying success and Solarized red carrying failure.

Personality lives in color, weather glyphs, and the day arc; structure stays stock macOS. The window is a native three-column `NavigationSplitView` with system toolbars, segmented pickers, grouped forms, and a system-glass sidebar. Density is standard Mac list density. Status is never color-only: every state has its own glyph and a text label.

Every color token resolves four ways (light, dark, Increase Contrast light, Increase Contrast dark) through `Solar.color`. The frontmatter records the light value; the sidecar carries all four.
keyCharacteristics: Solarized grounds: plate for the runs column, paper for output, settings, and the menu bar popover.
Weather glyphs carry run state, each in its status tint.
The day arc is the signature, above the runs list and in the menu bar popover.
Orange is the app accent only (selection and system controls).
Native controls, navigation, and keyboard behavior throughout.

rules.name: The Weather Rule
rules.body: Run state maps to exactly one hue: sun for passed, sky for running, storm for failed and interrupted, dusk for never run. Nothing else borrows these hues for decoration.

rules.name: The Accent Is Not Status Rule
rules.body: Orange (ember) is the accent for selection and controls only. It never marks a run state.

rules.name: The Four Appearances Rule
rules.body: A new color is a `Solar.color` with light, dark, and both Increase Contrast values, never a single hex.

rules.name: The Rounded Headings Rule
rules.body: `.fontDesign(.rounded)` goes on status and identity headings only; body, rows, and logs stay in default SF Pro.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Plate holds lists; paper holds content to read. A surface is one or the other, separated by a 1pt hairline, never a shadow.

dos: Do take every color from `Solar`, defined with light, dark, and Increase Contrast values.
Do pair every status color with its weather glyph and a text label.
Do use storm-text, not storm, for failure text.
Do use native SwiftUI controls, lists, forms, toolbars, and split views; put personality in color, glyphs, and the day arc.
Do gate continuous motion on Reduce Motion, as the running rays do.
Do separate surfaces with 1pt hairlines in hairline.
donts: Don't use orange (ember) for run state; running is sky, the next run is ink.
Don't use green checks or red crosses for status; the weather glyphs are the status vocabulary.
Don't add shadows or card elevation; use the plate and paper grounds.
Don't apply the rounded design to body text, rows, or logs.
